title: Grade 3 Science — Tue, Jun 10
description: Plant Kingdom — Day 2 of 5: Roots — types and functions
subject: science

questions.question: The two main types of roots are:
questions.explanation: Plants have either a tap root (one main thick root with smaller branches) or fibrous roots (many thin roots of equal size).

questions.question: A tap root has one main thick root that grows ____ and smaller roots from it.
questions.explanation: A tap root grows vertically down deep into the soil. Mango, neem, and gram plants have tap roots.

questions.question: Fibrous roots are:
options: Many thin roots of similar size spreading from the base of the stem
Roots that grow above the ground
questions.explanation: Fibrous roots form a dense mat of many thin equal roots, like in grass, wheat, and rice.

questions.question: Which plant has a tap root?
questions.explanation: Carrot has a tap root that stores food and grows deep into the soil. We eat the carrot root.

questions.question: Which plant has fibrous roots?
questions.explanation: Grass has fibrous roots — a dense network of thin roots that spread near the surface of the soil.

questions.question: Roots help the plant by anchoring it to the soil. This means roots:
options: Hold the plant firm so it does not fall
questions.explanation: Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil, preventing it from being uprooted by wind or rain.

questions.question: Roots also absorb ____ and ____ from the soil for the plant.
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals (nutrients) from the soil, which the plant needs to grow.

questions.question: Which of these is a root that we eat as food?
questions.explanation: Radish is a tap root that we eat as a vegetable. Other edible roots include carrot, beet, and turnip.

questions.question: The tiny hair-like parts near the tip of a root are called:
questions.explanation: Root hairs are tiny extensions near the root tip. They greatly increase the area for absorbing water and minerals.

questions.question: Why do fibrous roots prevent soil erosion better than tap roots?
options: They grow deeper into the soil
They spread widely and hold soil particles together near the surface
questions.explanation: Fibrous roots spread in all directions near the surface, binding soil particles and stopping rain from washing the soil away.

questions.question: The banyan tree grows roots from its branches that reach the ground. These are called:
questions.explanation: Banyan tree branches grow prop roots (aerial roots) that reach down into the ground to support the wide branches.

questions.question: A plant that grows in desert stores water in its roots. This is an example of a ____ root.
questions.explanation: Some plants store food or water in modified (storage) roots. Examples: sweet potato, radish, carrot.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT describe a function of roots?
questions.explanation: Making food (photosynthesis) is done by leaves, not roots. Roots anchor, absorb water, and sometimes store food.

questions.question: Rice and wheat have ____ roots.
questions.explanation: Cereals like rice and wheat have fibrous root systems — many thin roots spreading from the base of the stem.

questions.question: The main difference between tap root and fibrous root is:
options: Tap root is green; fibrous root is brown
Tap root has one thick main root; fibrous root has many thin equal roots
Only fibrous roots anchor the plant
questions.explanation: The key difference: tap root = one dominant main root with side branches; fibrous root = many thin roots of similar size.
